title: Two-Face: Combining Collective and One-Sided Communication for Efficient Distributed SpMM
problem: Distributed SpMM execution faces a fundamental trade-off: collective communication causes inefficiency from unnecessary data transfers, while fine-grained sparsity-aware one-sided communication incurs prohibitive software overhead.
motivation: SpMM is widely used in scientific computing and graph neural networks, making efficient distributed execution critical for practical applications.
method: Two-Face identifies which parts of the matrix contain lots of data (dense) and which are mostly empty (sparse), then adapts its communication strategy: broadcasting to all processors for dense parts, or sending data directly between only needed processors for sparse parts. Broadcasting sends redundant data but requires no coordination; direct communication avoids redundancy but requires careful scheduling. By choosing the strategy based on each part's density, Two-Face minimizes the combined cost of wasted data and coordination overhead.
key_novelty: Dynamically switching between broadcast and point-to-point communication based on whether each region is dense or sparse, to simultaneously minimize redundant data transfers and scheduling overhead.
contributions: Hybrid communication framework combining collectives and one-sided patterns for efficient distributed SpMM
Analysis of communication cost trade-offs between sparsity-aware and sparsity-unaware approaches
Runtime system for adaptive communication pattern selection based on sparsity characteristics
primary_theme: Adaptive hybrid communication for sparse distributed computation
